key_insight: Cu feedstock morphology governs impact deformation in cold-sprayed Cu–Al₂O₃ composites: spherical particles localize strain at splat interfaces, while spongy particles distribute strain through ligament collapse.
engineering_relevance: Powder morphology offers a design lever alongside spray parameters for tailoring ceramic encapsulation, microstructure, and deposit mechanical performance.
method: Compare spherical and spongy Cu feedstocks in cold-sprayed Cu–Al₂O₃ deposits.
Evaluate mechanical and tribological behavior using micro-compression and tribological tests.
evidence_signal: Multiscale characterization links spherical Cu to bimodal grain structures balancing strength and ductility, and spongy Cu to distributed strain hardening and enhanced ceramic encapsulation.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance gains or processing window, limiting direct translation into production specifications.
paper_title: Feedstock morphology governs impact-induced deformation in cold sprayed metal-ceramic composites
